title: Tenant path economics ledger and decomposer service
creator: Rina Kapoor
description:
Build a backend service ("ledger") that computes per-tenant, per-path (route -> model variant -> device class) cost and latency breakdowns for the Console and downstream billing/alerts. This service will consume inference telemetry and serving instrumentation and produce both near-real-time (1m/5m windows) and daily rollups. Goals:

- Provide deterministic, explainable cost/latency attributions for each tenant and route that the Console can display and export.
- Capture serving-level factors: model variant, quantization profile, GPU type, batching behavior, KV cache hits, routing fallbacks, and any retry/fallback overhead.
- Support queries by time range, dimensions (route, model, region, pool), and aggregation level (per-request, per-minute, hourly).
- Be efficient in storage and compute: use streaming pre-aggregation for high-cardinality dims and offline recomputation for full-precision reconstructions.

Scope and constraints:
- Input sources: kafka://inference.events (per-request instrumentation), kafka://inference.metrics (per-token resource counts), and redis/cache hit logs.
- Output: materialized minute/hour/day rollups in clickhouse for Console queries, parquet daily archives in S3 for audits, and a metrics-backed API for Programmatic exports.
- Accuracy targets: aggregated cost < 1.5% error vs ground-truth hourly ledger; p95 latency estimates within 5% of true p95 when using online approximations.

Design summary:
1) Streaming ingest: lightweight GO consumer that normalizes events, enriches with model metadata, and writes event-keys to a Kafka intermediate topic with schema v1 (proto).
2) Real-time aggregator: Flink job (stateful) that maintains windowed aggregations (1m/5m) and emits pre-aggregated rows to ClickHouse and a short-term RocksDB state backend for fast recompute. Uses TDigest for latency distributions and HyperLogLog sketches for unique route-cardinality where needed.
3) Offline recompute: Spark job that consumes raw event archives daily to produce canonical rollups and reconcile drift from streaming approximations.
4) API and UI: new Console endpoints to fetch per-tenant breakdowns and an export job to produce itemized CSVs for finance teams.

Trade-offs and decisions so far:
- Precision vs cost: we accept small streaming approximation error (TDigest/HLL) in exchange for sub-minute UI responsiveness. Full precision hourly/daily reconciles will be used for billing-grade exports.
- Cardinality handling: drop extremely low-volume route-model combos from minute-level materializations and track them only in daily archives to bound ClickHouse partitions.
- Attribution model: attribute shared overhead (routing/queue wait) proportionally by per-request token counts rather than equal-split to better reflect economic impact.

Success metrics:
- Console latency for breakdown endpoints < 300ms for 1m rollup queries.
- Consistency: streaming vs offline diffs < 1.5% for top-95% of tenants by spend.
- Adoption: replace legacy per-route aggregator for 80% of Console breakdown traffic in first month after GA.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal-only with synthetic tenants + 2 pilot customers; run both old aggregator and new ledger in parallel.
- Beta: enable for 25% of tenants (low-risk segment) with canary alerts and automated rollback.
- GA: full migration and deprecation of legacy aggregator; provide export of historical rollups for audits.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Drift alert when streaming/offline reconciliation exceeds 2% for > 2 hours.
- Backpressure alerting on Kafka consumer lag and Flink state growth.
- SLA monitors for API latency and ClickHouse query tail latencies.
